Carlos A. Gimenez criticizes Cuban government and highlights U.S. sanctions in recent tweets
U.S. Congressman Carlos A. Gimenez addressed recent developments regarding Cuba through several tweets posted on September 30 and October 1, highlighting new U.S. sanctions against the Cuban government and denouncing legal action against activists...
U.S. Congressman Carlos A. Gimenez, who represents Florida’s 28th district and was born in Havana, Cuba, posted a series of tweets on September 30 and October 1, 2026, addressing the political situation in Cuba and recent U.S. actions targeting the Cuban government.
On September 30, Gimenez wrote: "#SOSCuba The despicable dictatorship in Havana has its days numbered. Every day, @StateDept & @USTreasury collaborate to hold the regime’s thugs accountable. The latest sanctions ensure the regime has fewer resources to oppress the people of #Cuba! https://t.co/0qEQ0uYztr".
In a tweet dated October 1, he continued: "#SOSCuba La dictadura castrista pretende llevar a juicio a dos patriotas: Anna Bensi, una joven de apenas 21 años, y a su madre. ¿Su “delito”? Grabar a un represor del régimen que llegó a su casa con una citación de la Seguridad del Estado. ¡Desde el Congreso de Estados".
Later that same day, Gimenez announced an upcoming media appearance: "NEWS —> I’ll be on @FoxBusiness shortly with @Varneyco! Tune in!".
Gimenez has served in Congress since 2021 after replacing Debbie Mucarsel-Powell and previously held positions in the Florida House of Representatives as well as the Miami-Dade County Commission from 2005 to 2011. He is an alumnus of Barry University (1999) and currently resides in Miami.
The U.S. State Department and Treasury have implemented new sanctions aimed at limiting resources available to the Cuban government for internal repression—a policy stance supported by Gimenez's public statements.
